basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 10.' and it opens '(Vers. 10.) Et fuit, inquit, caput regni ipsius Babel et Arach, et Achad, et Chalanne in'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 10.) Et fuit, inquit, caput regni ipsius Babel et Arach, et Achad, et Chalanne in terra Sennaar. Nemrod, filius Chus, arripuit insuetam primus in populo tyrannidem, regnavitque in Babylone, quae ab eo, quod ibi confusae sunt linguae turrim aedificantium, BABEL (בבל) appellata est. Babel enim interpretatur confusio. Regnavit autem et in Arach, hoc est, in Edissa, et in Achad, quae nunc dicitur Nisibis: et in Chalanne, quae postea verso nomine a Seleuco rege est dicta Seleucia, vel certe quae nunc Κτησιφὼν appellatur.
